subject: Archaeology
title: The Oldowan Toolkit: First Technology
description: One-minute skill: The Oldowan Toolkit: First Technology.

hook.text: The oldest known stone tools are 3.3 million years old. They were made before our genus Homo even existed.

buildup.text: Oldowan tools from Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania are simple cobbles with a few flakes knocked off to create an edge.

discovery.text: Experiments show it takes real skill to knap stone consistently. Early toolmakers understood angles and fracture lines.

twist.text: Chimpanzees use rocks to crack nuts but cannot produce sharp flakes. The leap to stone tools was a cognitive revolution.

climax.text: Oldowan technology stayed unchanged for over a million years. The first invention was also the longest lasting.

punchline.text: The first technology lasted a million years. Your phone lasts two.

quiz.question: What makes Oldowan stone tools significant?
options: They are the most complex stone tools ever discovered
They are the oldest known tools and lasted over a million years unchanged
They were the first tools made from metal instead of wood
